url: self-captured, session-02, device clock 20:51; ~74 device px of travel moved 2 trading days
notes: STAR EVIDENCE FOR PRIMITIVE P1 (cursor-based placement). This is the SAME interaction grammar as drawing placement: a draggable on-chart cursor with a live readout, rather than a numeric input. TradingView solves the fat-finger problem by making the readout continuous, so the user corrects by feel instead of by precision. UCT has no equivalent cursor primitive anywhere on mobile.

action: Tap the scissors glyph at the midpoint of the select-bar cursor
response: The chart is CUT at that bar: history to the left is kept, everything right of the cut disappears, a large 'Replay' watermark with a rewind glyph is drawn across the chart centre, the last price becomes the cut bar's close (302.25) and the Sell / Buy buttons become ENABLED (red and blue filled)
result: STAR THE SCISSORS HANDLE IS THE COMMIT - it converts a proposed cut into an active replay session
notes: STAR NEW ROW, and the key discoverability finding for replay. The cut is committed by tapping a GLYPH ON THE CHART, not by a toolbar button - so a user who never notices the small scissors icon can drag the cursor forever and never start a replay. Confirmed empirically: with Select bar armed but uncommitted, Play and Step remain DISABLED. That is a real discoverability defect worth naming, and the counter-argument is that the scissors metaphor is unusually legible once seen.

action: Toggle Select bar off, then on again
response: Off: the cursor and date badge disappear and the full live chart is restored. On again: the cursor reappears at the DEFAULT position (Thu 13 Aug 26), NOT at the position it was dragged to (Tue 11 Aug 26)
result: TOGGLING SELECT-BAR MODE DISCARDS THE CHOSEN BAR
notes: NEW ROW - a small state-loss defect found by direct experiment. A user who arms replay, carefully drags to a bar, accidentally taps the mode toggle, and re-arms, silently loses the position with no warning. Root cause STATE_PERSISTENCE. Low severity but a genuine papercut and exactly the class of thing the master prompt asks for.

response: An ANCHORED POPOVER (not a bottom sheet) opens upward from the toolbar, titled 'Replay speed', listing NINE values: 10x (checkmarked), 7x, 5x, 3x, 1x, 0.5x, 0.3x, 0.2x, 0.1x
result: NINE REPLAY SPEEDS, DEFAULT 10x, SELECTED BY CHECKMARK
notes: NEW ROW. TWO things worth carrying into UCT: (a) the full desktop speed ladder ships to the phone with no reduction - same pattern as the 21 chart types (TYPE-0077); (b) selection here is a CHECKMARK, whereas the interval sheet (TF-0074) and chart-type grid (TYPE-0083) encode selection by FILL COLOUR ALONE. So TradingView's own selection language splits by control shape: list popover = checkmark, chip grid = fill. The colour-only variants remain the accessibility concern; this row is the proof that the app already owns a better pattern internally.

result: STAR FOUR WAYS TO PLACE THE REPLAY START, PLUS TWO MOBILE-ONLY CHROME TOGGLES
notes: STAR THE RICHEST SINGLE MENU FOUND IN THE REPLAY AREA. 'Random bar' is a blind-practice mode - the feature serious backtesters ask for, shipped on a phone. 'Select the first available date' means you can replay a symbol from the beginning of its history. AND 'Show the tab bar' is a MOBILE-SPECIFIC DENSITY CONTROL: TradingView lets the user hide the app's own bottom tab bar to reclaim chart height during replay. That is a phone-native affordance with no desktop analogue and it is the clearest evidence that replay was re-thought for mobile rather than ported.

action: Compare the header change value against the replayed last price
response: The last price tracks the replay (302.25, then 305.93) but the change and percent beside it stay FROZEN at the live-session values '-8.24 (-2.51%)' for the whole replay
result: DEFECT: THE HEADER CHANGE/PERCENT DOES NOT FOLLOW THE REPLAY
notes: STAR GENUINE BUG FOUND IN A COMPETITOR (master prompt S31 edge cases). During replay the header reads a price from the replayed past next to a change computed from the live present, so the two halves of one line disagree. A user reading '305.93 -8.24 (-2.51%)' would compute a prior close of 314.17, which is not the replayed prior close. Small, but it is a real correctness defect in the flagship product and it is worth recording so the parity matrix is honest in BOTH directions.

action: Tap the X in the replay toolbar
response: A NATIVE iOS UIAlertController appears - title 'Confirmation', body 'Do you want to exit Bar Replay mode for AAPL?', buttons Cancel / OK. Tapping OK restores the full live chart with all indicators and the replay toolbar removed.
result: STAR EXIT IS GUARDED BY A NATIVE iOS ALERT, AND THE ALERT IS SYMBOL-SCOPED
notes: STAR TWO FINDINGS IN ONE. (a) TradingView mobile is overwhelmingly a WEB-RENDERED chart inside a native shell, and this is one of the few places it reaches for a genuine UIAlertController - reserved for destructive confirmation. (b) The copy names the SYMBOL ('for AAPL'), which means replay state is tracked PER SYMBOL, not per chart. UCT COMPARISON: UCT mobile has no destructive-action confirmation pattern at all; its sheets commit on a single tap (SET-0030). Root cause for UCT = MISSING_CAPABILITY.

action: Observe the chart toolbar undo arrow while replay is active
response: The undo arrow greys out for the duration of the replay session and returns on exit
notes: NEW ROW. Correct modal discipline: replay is a MODE, and the app disables the global history stack inside it rather than letting undo half-unwind a replay. Relevant to UNDO area as well as REPLAY.

action: Look for any replay capability in the UCT mobile chart shell
response: MobileChartToolbar.jsx exposes exactly five doors - timeframe, chart type, indicators, watchlist, more. There is no replay entry point, no replay component under pages/charts/mobile/, and no replay concept in StockChart.jsx.
result: UCT HAS NO BAR REPLAY ON ANY PLATFORM
notes: UCT COMPARISON ROW. PARITY = MISSING. ROOT CAUSE = MISSING_CAPABILITY, and NOT a mobile-presentation gap - UCT's desktop chart has no replay either, so this is a product-scope decision rather than a phone regression. SEVERITY: P2 for the stated audience. Worth noting that lightweight-charts CAN support a naive replay cheaply (truncate the series and step setData), so a minimal Select-bar + Play + Step would not require the engine work that the exotic chart types (UCT-TYPE-0001) would. The expensive part is the paper-trading strip, which should be scoped out of any v1.
